title: Jung Woo-sung's Beat Comic To Premiere As 10-Episode Drama In 2026
text:
Jung Woo-sung’s Beat Comic To Premiere As 10-Episode Drama In 2026
The CEO of ALT Studio opened up about debuting with a 10-episode drama series based on Beat, the iconic youth noir comic.
Korean dramas and comic strips are enjoyed around the world, with their immense power to evoke a sense of emotion among the audience. One such youth noir comic, Beat, by legendary South Korean manhwa artist Heo Young Man, which went on to become iconic over the years, is set to get a drama remake with ALT Studio’s debut project. Now, one of the officials from the newly established production company confirmed the development.
In a statement by ALT Studio’s CEO Kim Young Bae, the newly established production company announced their debut project based on the legendary Beat. “Our first project will be a 10-episode drama adaptation of ‘Beat,’ based on the comic of the same name by Heo Young Man," revealed the statement.
Recommended Stories
The upcoming drama series has sparked a sense of curiosity among the fans. Based on the comic by Korean comic giant Heo Young Man, the drama will reportedly evoke deep nostalgia for the old generation as it will reinterpret the spirit of 1990s youth in a modern context. Undoubtedly, there has been an anticipation about the cast who will represent today’s teens and twenties.
More focus is on the lead character Min, originally portrayed by the now 52-year-old actor Jung Woo Sung, known for his notable works in films and television shows like The Good, the Bad, the Weird, Asura: The City of Madness, Innocent Witness, Steel Rain, Asphalt Man, Padam Padam and Tell Me That You Love Me, among others.
What is Beat and Beat Syndrome?
Heo Young Man’s Beat explores themes of anger, confusion, frustration, and growing pains among young people in Korea. The noir-style comic sold over a million copies when serialised from 1994 to 1995, courtesy of its noir-style tone and storytelling. Additionally, it sparked a cultural phenomenon called Beat syndrome with its trendy props of the story, like the Honda CBR600F motorcycle, Zippo lighters, and Marlboro Reds.
Previous adaptations of Beat
In 1997, Beat was adapted into a film directed by Kim Sung Soo. It starred Jung Woo Sung and Ko So Young in lead roles, garnering immense praise and a lasting impact. The film also cemented the Tell Me That You Love Me star’s status as a youth icon of the 1990s.
About ALT Studio
ALT Studio, founded by renowned producers known for dramas like Taxi Driver 1 & 2, My ID is Gangnam Beauty and others, are set to showcase their work while preserving the emotion of original projects while providing relatable themes for the youth with their reimagination of Beat.
